post.summary: Refresh account statements
post.description: ## Refresh account statements Refreshes account with the latest statements from the bank account. ## Params **bankAccountId**: Id of the bank account to be refreshed. **requestParts**: List of accounts to be refreshed. - **accountId**: Account id to be refreshed. - **pullIndex**: Represents the month to be refreshed. - Ex. 1= last month, 2= two months, 3= three months ago and so on. - Min/Max allowed: 1-6 ***Only 1 refresh is allowed per bank account in a period of 24 hours.** ## Handling response with MFA (Multi Factor Authentication) Some accounts are configured with MFA to improve security, so if you get a MFA challenge (Http Code - 203) you need to render the questions in your app and call **/api/v2/statements/refresh/mfa** with a proper answer. ## MFA Challenge types - **text**: Challenge text. E.g *Enter name of your first pet*. - **image**: Base64 encoded image with text to be rendered by your application. E.g. *data:image/png;base64,/9j/4AAQSkZJRgABAQAAAQABAAD/...* - **choices**: Multiple choice challenge with text/value. - **imageChoices**: Multiple choice challenge with base64 image/value.

203.description: Some statements require MFA. Need to call */api/v2/statements/refresh/mfa* with the answer to the MFA challenge

post.summary: Refresh bank statements with MFA
post.description:
## Refresh account statements with MFA (Multi Factor Authentication)

This API should be called only when the call to **/api/v2/statements/refresh** returns a MFA challenge, Http code: **203** or when the call to this API returns another MFA challenge.

## Params

**bankAccountId**: Id of the bank account to be refreshed.
**accountId**: Id of the account to be refreshed.
**pullIndex**: Represents the month to be refreshed. Please use the same value provided during the call to **/api/v2/statements/refresh**.
**mfaRequest**: MFA challenge that could be a simple question, an image, a multiple choice question or multiple images.
- **mfaSession**: Provided in the response of **/api/v2/statements/refresh**
 - **mfaBody**: Wrapper for questions.
    - **questions**: Represents different types of challenges.
        - **text**: Challenge text. E.g *Enter name of your first pet*.
        - **image**: Not required.
        - **choices**: Not required.
        - **imageChoices**: Not required.
        - **answer**: Answer to the question in text format.

post.summary: OCR a PDF bank statement and return extracted transactions as JSON
post.description:
Runs the standard bank-statement OCR pipeline (Gemini Vision / Google Document OCR) against the uploaded PDF and returns the extracted transactions plus reconciliation status.

Files larger than 20 MB are processed asynchronously: the response returns `async_processing=true` with no transactions, and a download link is emailed to the address provided in the `email` form field. The `email` parameter is required for files larger than 20 MB.

200.description:
Returns the add account URL widget to be invoked by the client

Set the optional **source** field to **MX** to connect a bank via MX (for banks Finicity does not support); omit it (or use FINICITY) for the default Finicity flow. When **source=MX**, widgetUrl is an MX Connect URL (moneydesktop.com) loaded with the MX Connect widget instead of the Finicity SDK; omit institutionId to let the user search for their bank in the widget.

Call */api/v2/institutions/provider-options* first if you do not already know which provider covers the bank.

When the call succeed, returning code 200, grab the content of widgetUrl and make a call to this url

get.description:
Lists the institutions supported by a given bank-data provider.

Set **source** to **MX** to search the banks reachable through MX (useful for banks Finicity does not support); omit it (or use FINICITY) for the default Finicity catalog.

**name** filters by institution name. Each entry's **id** is the value to pass as **institutionId** when calling */api/v2/account/add*, and **allowStatements** tells whether that institution delivers statements — pick the institution before connecting so statements are requested at connect time.

get.summary: Find which providers cover a bank
get.description:
Answers *which provider should I connect this bank through* - call this before */api/v2/account/add* or */api/v2/account/add/lite*.

**name** searches bank names as free text. Each entry is one bank at one provider, carrying the **source** and the **id** to pass together as **source** and **institutionId** on the add call, plus **allowTransactions** and **allowStatements** so the provider that delivers the data you need can be picked.

A bank reachable through two providers appears twice, once per **source**, and either may be used. An **id** is only valid for the **source** listed beside it.

Unlike */api/v2/institutions*, which lists one provider's catalog at a time, this covers every provider in a single call.

source.description: Bank-data provider: FINICITY (default) or MX. Omit for Finicity.
Bank-data provider: FINICITY (default) or MX. Omit for Finicity.

Bank-data provider: FINICITY (default) or MX. Omit for Finicity. Applies to both /api/v2/account/add and /api/v2/account/add/lite. Use /api/v2/institutions/provider-options to find which providers cover a given bank.

id.description: LedgerSync transaction id. Ids are numbered separately per source, so store the id together with the source, or use transactionId.

transactionId.description: The source and the id together, for example FINICITY_119874 or MX_628988. Unique across sources.

transactionHash.description: FINICITY only; null for MX. A 32-character hash of the transaction's details that stays the same when a connection is disconnected and reconnected. Use it to match transactions across a reconnect; two identical purchases on the same day share it.

postedDate.description: The day the bank posted the transaction. The format depends on the source: FINICITY and FDE send yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss in UTC with no offset (read the first 10 characters as the date), MX sends MM/dd/yyyy. Null on FINICITY pending transactions. On MX pending transactions it holds the transaction date.

bankAccountId.description: FINICITY: the provider's account id. MX: the LedgerSync connection id (banks[].id in the account list). FDE: the account code.

accountId.description: The LedgerSync account id, the same id as in the account list (banks[].accounts[].id).

status.description: FINICITY: active, pending or shadow. MX: POSTED or PENDING. FDE: as FDE reports it.

transactionDate.description: The day the transaction happened as the bank reports it (for a card, the purchase date). Same format rules as postedDate. LedgerSync passes the bank's value through unchanged.

type.description: As the institution reports it. MX sends DEBIT or CREDIT.

amount.description: Signed amount: negative means money out of the account.

totalItems.description: Number of matching transactions across all pages.

selectedPage.description: The page returned, starting at 0. A page past the end returns an empty list.

source.description: Bank-data provider: FINICITY (default) or MX. Takes precedence over addOn.

id.description: Pass this value as institutionId when adding an account with the same source.

source.description: Bank-data provider this institution is reachable through.

allowStatements.description: Whether this institution delivers statements through the given provider.

allowTransactions.description: Whether this institution delivers transactions through the given provider.

totalItems.description: Total rows available to page through for this search.

truncated.description: True when the search matched more banks than could be returned. The answer is a prefix rather than the whole set; narrow name rather than paging further.

institutions.description: One entry per bank and provider pair. A bank reachable through two providers appears twice, once per source, and either may be used to connect it.

id.description: LedgerSync account id. Send it as accountId to the transaction list.

accountId.description: The provider's own id for this account. Use id to identify the account in LedgerSync.

id.description: Connection id. Numbered separately per source.

transactionUpdateStatus.description: Result of the latest transaction refresh, for example UPDATED or FAILED. FAILED together with transactionErrorMessage means the connection needs attention; its stored transactions are still returned by the transaction list.

source.description: The data provider of this connection: FINICITY, MX, FDE or PDF. Send it as source to the transaction list for this connection's accounts. PDF connections are not served by the transaction list.

Which provider this connection is on: FINICITY, MX, FDE or PDF. The same value the account list returns for this connection, and the value to send as the source parameter on the other per-connection calls.

bankAccount.description: The provider's own identifier for this connection: the institution login id for Finicity, the member guid for MX, the account code for FDE.

addedBy.description: Username of the accounting firm the connection was added under, recorded when the connection was created: the firm itself when the firm owns the connection, otherwise the client's firm. It is not the person who completed the bank login. For FDE connections it is the username of the connection's owner.

accountCode.description: FDE connections only: the FDE account code, the same value as bankAccount. Omitted for Finicity and MX connections, whose identifier is in bankAccount.
